title: A3 homepage: Association for Advancing Automation's automation hub landing page
answer: The Association for Advancing Automation, known as A3, publishes this landing page at automate.org. It is a short introduction to the association rather than a report, and it states that A3 brings together robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI as a hub for information on those technologies. The most useful thing it says is that A3 positions itself as connecting innovators, businesses and technologies across robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI to accelerate progress in automation. No data, dates or figures appear.

sections.body: This is the landing page of automate.org, published by A3, the Association for Advancing Automation. It is a short introductory page for the association itself rather than a report, study or article, and it describes the technology areas A3 covers and the role it claims in the automation sector. No publication date, author or revision date is stated in the text. The text was harvested on 2026-09-28, which is a capture date rather than a stated publication date. The scope is limited to describing the organisation and its subject areas.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The harvested text is short and largely repetitive. It presents A3, the Association for Advancing Automation, as a body that combines robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI into what it calls a comprehensive hub for information on the latest technologies. That same sentence appears twice in the harvested text, which suggests a tagline reused across the page rather than new content. A second sentence describes the association's purpose, connecting innovators, businesses and technologies across key technology sectors, named here as robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI, to accelerate progress in automation. The two lists of sectors do not match exactly. The first includes imaging and motors and mentions AI without qualifying it, while the second drops imaging and motors and refers specifically to industrial AI. Nothing else is offered. There is no description of membership, no research, no order statistics, no events calendar and no explanation of how the named sectors relate to one another. The page works as a signpost to a wider site rather than as a document that can be read on its own.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, percentages, dates or statistics of any kind. The claims it does make are two. First, that A3 combines robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI into a comprehensive hub for information on the latest technologies. Second, that A3 connects innovators, businesses and technologies across robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI to accelerate progress in automation. Both are statements of the association's own scope and purpose, not findings or measurements.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in manufacturing would use this page only as a pointer. It identifies A3 as an organisation whose stated remit covers robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI, which are the technology areas that sit alongside factory automation, so it is a reasonable starting point for finding that organisation's other material. It does not itself support any claim about deployment, adoption or measurement. The text does not mention order statistics, robotics deployment figures, machine-vision integration or sensor density, so it cannot be cited for those points on its own. Anyone citing A3 for quarterly order statistics would need a different page from the same publisher.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Manufacturing

sections.body: This is a landing page with very little substance. It carries no date, no author, no methodology and no data, and it does not discuss manufacturing as a sector at all. It is the association's own site describing the association, so it is self-descriptive rather than independent. The two sentences it contains overlap and disagree slightly on which sectors are included. It should be treated as a signpost to A3's other publications, not as evidence for anything about AI in manufacturing.
